Counter Culture states a 50/50 bean blend, but that is not a measured half-caffeine cup. The exact decaf component and roast wording deserve a bag-date check.

segments.source: Fast Forward is a sensible first bag for someone wanting a medium, nutty-and-sweet daily coffee across drip and occasional espresso. Its year-round name does not mean a fixed farm mix. Buy it for the roaster’s steady flavor aim, then check the actual roast-date composition and your own cup.

segments.source: Gradient is the dark-roast option for a buyer who wants chocolate and nuts but does not rule out a berry signal. The Colombian sourcing and washed-process statement make its identity clearer than a generic dark bag, while the rotating components and your actual brew still matter.

Equator Blend is a practical one-bag candidate for medium-dark drip and French press, with an unusually detailed current origin panel and Equator’s own cream-and-sugar positioning. The page also offers espresso grind, but gives filter recipes rather than a portafilter target; espresso buyers should be ready to dial in without a roaster shot recipe.

segments.source: Eye of the Tiger is the adventurous espresso choice: Equator gives a medium-light roast, current Costa Rican and Rwandan component detail, and an 18 g to 46 g starting shot. Its seasonal profile can change, so the recipe and the bag must be checked together rather than assuming one permanent origin list.
